<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"mitsevox"} -->
_Requested by **Lucas** · [project
thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01SU1kLYmWeT4ejAYnBNpQjs?thread=cmsg_01SU1kLYmWeT4ejAYnBNpQjs9tHa7woX9xn9uXyAo2CtXi)_

## Scope

Implements the CI speed-up plan in one PR, as the owner asked (owner
decisions 2026-10-25: PRs may reuse main-produced hash-keyed results
that main audits; PRs skip the host re-check). Tools, workflow, focused
regression tests and cache-operation documentation:
`.github/workflows/baseline.yml`, `tools/activity.py`,
`tools/source_build.py`, `tools/function_compare.py`,
`tools/matching.py`, `tools/ci_policy.py`, tests. No source, config or
ledger changes.

1. **Provenance fetch.** Missing pinned commits arrive in one `git fetch
--filter=blob:none`, and the checks read tree entries from parent trees
(fresh clone: 90 commits, ~2 s; was one fetch per commit). Side effect:
that fetch sets `remote.origin.promisor` and `partialclonefilter` in the
checkout's config, so a later git command that needs one of those
commits' blobs would fetch it on demand. It only runs with
`--fetch-provenance`, the CI-host flag, and CI discards its checkout.
2. **Credit check.** `prefetch()` answers the per-entry Git questions
with batched `cat-file` calls and, on merge-free revisions, one
`diff-tree` walk that reproduces `git rev-list REV -- path` (equal for
all 945 ledger paths on main). On merge revisions it runs the per-path
`rev-list`s in a pool. Anything not proven there is re-asked one by one,
so every error keeps its message and order. Both attribution passes stay
as before: the PR's own revision and the synthetic squash, compared with
each other.
3. **Parallel compile** of linked units. Folding, retained layout and
the link stay sequential in manifest order, and any staging or compile
failure is raised at its unit's turn.
4. **Host re-check** (second live-receipt export) runs on main, and on
any PR proof that reused nothing. Other host unit tests still run on
every PR.
5. **Ledger first.** `activity.py --ledger-only REV [--squash-base B]`
runs all ledger/Git attribution checks (both passes) before the compiler
setup.
6. **Checkout unchanged.** Limiting refs to main leaves 620 provenance
commits missing instead of 90 (60 s fetch); `fetch-depth: 0` stays.
7. **Measurement cache.** Each comparison unit's measurement is keyed by
its object hash, its configured placement, the addresses its symbols
resolve to, the linked source it overlaps, the target and the measuring
tools. PRs restore entries and linked outputs, which
`function_compare.load()` validates like fresh ones.
8. **Compile cache.** Linked and comparison objects are reused while
compiler, flags, include path, compile directory, source, every recorded
dependency and every repository symlink are unchanged and no same-named
file (ignoring case) appeared that could shadow an include.

Trust model: one `build/cache` Actions cache, saved only by a full main
push or explicitly requested full main audit dispatch. Main compiles and
measures everything fresh, fails on any cached result that disagrees,
then replaces the cache. A PR proof that reused anything is not handed
to main for publication, so main rebuilds from scratch (and audits) on
every such merge; a PR proof that reused nothing stays publishable
exactly as today.

## Evidence and validation

- CI green on every head; 722b447: 4.7 min, f7e07ff: 4.0 min, both with
cold caches (median before: 7.4 min). Warm-cache timings on CI exist
only after main has saved its first cache (PR runs never write one).
- Local, 4 cores, at f7e07ff: a fully cached run (source build and
matching in use mode, export with squash preflight) gives byte-identical
`build/source/report.json`, `build/matching/report.json`,
`build/site/activity.json`, `build/site/progress.json` (`built_at`
masked) and `build/GN7E69/report.json` to a from-scratch run. Audit mode
on an existing cache audited every unit (457 linked objects, 524
comparison objects, 524 measurements) with no differences.
- Local timings: source build 47 s → 17 s fresh, 10 s cached; matching
50 s → 18 s cached; export with squash preflight 52 s → ~20 s;
ledger-only check ~2 s on a fresh clone, ~5 s on a merge revision.
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: OK. New tests cover tree
lookups vs `cat-file --batch-check` (including `//`, `./`, `..`), the
tree walk vs `rev-list` (including former directories), prefetch vs
one-by-one answers, cache reuse, audit disagreement, include shadowing,
symlinks, path escapes, and the receipts lane.

## Integration follow-through

Fixed the hosted bootstrap gap at
`a395d15091b431d5cd142151bb3aa8a28ddc842f`: a cold PR can publish a
reusable proof, leaving main with no reason to run/cache an audit.
Baseline now offers the boolean opt-in `audit_build_cache` (default
false). On main, requesting it bypasses proof selection, forces complete
fresh validation/audit and permits saving the resulting cache.
Default/branch dispatches and PRs cannot save. CONTRIBUTING.md documents
the one-time seed command and trust boundary. Cache algorithms and
original reviewed optimization remain unchanged.

Focused policy/cache/activity/publication tests pass (83 tests, one
skipped), including seven cases evaluating the actual workflow
select/save guards. Final CI40231990816 is running. After merge: run
explicit main seed/audit once, then rerun this PR's same-head CI and
record hosted cache-hit counts/timing. Hosted warm behavior is not yet
claimed. Earlier cold timings and local warm equivalence above remain
historical evidence, not a substitute for that hosted test.
